accuracy.evidence: Checked against NGSS 4-PS3-3 (changes in energy when objects collide; clarification: energy transfer to the other object, sound, heat) and 4-PS3-1 (speed relates to energy), plus the NGSS 4-PS3 disciplinary core ideas PS3.A, PS3.B and PS3.C. Equal-mass head-on collisions of hard spheres exchange nearly all motion (the first marble 'almost stops', wording chosen because real marbles roll and lose a little). Cup slide 6/12/18 cm for 10/20/30 cm is labelled a model; it is consistent with the ball's kinetic energy at the bottom scaling with height and the cup's sliding distance scaling with the energy it receives. Bounce heights from 100 cm: tennis ball 55 cm is inside the ITF rebound rule (135–147 cm from 254 cm, 53–58%); a high-bounce rubber ball about 80%; clay about 0. Bumper squash distances (0.2, 2, 5 cm) and relative pushes (25×, 2.5×, 1×) follow average force = energy ÷ stopping distance for the same energy, presented only as relative bars. The text says these are typical model values.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented energy misconceptions for this age (Driver et al. 1994 Making Sense of Secondary Science, energy chapter; AAAS Project 2061 energy misconception items; Watts 1983 frameworks): energy is used up or lost in a crash, a faster object pushes less because it rushes past, still objects have moving energy, same-size marbles stick or both stop, a small marble on a heavy ball, energy destroyed by the floor, and squashy padding 'wastes' energy rather than softening the stop. Each appears in a prediction, a lab message or challenge feedback.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab, including flag_kemv.js (kinetic energy depends on mass and speed), flag_energy.js (skate-ramp stores), flag_ramp.js (rolling down slopes), flag_coll.js (collision theory in chemistry) and flag_ename.js (naming energy types). Only this lab passes motion between equal marbles, measures a cup's slide from three ramp heights, hunts the energy signs in a crash scene with distractors, compares three bounce heights and tests squashing bumpers on an egg rider.

lab_teaches.evidence: Six steps: gentle and hard rolls into a still marble (drag back to set speed), three ramp heights into a cup with a results row, four energy signs plus two distractors (red paint, ceiling lamp) in a crash scene, three balls dropped from 1 m with a height scale, three bumpers with a push meter and a cracked or safe egg, then the challenge. The banners state the rule only after the task is complete.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: the equal-marble collision ('both stop', 'they stick'), a higher ramp start ('slides less, because the ball rushes past'), and the clay ball's energy ('it was destroyed', 'no energy when it falls'). The reveal names the learner's own choice after the task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages: speed ignored, fast means less push, energy used up, energy still in a stopped car, heavy means no energy, energy destroyed, marbles stick, bouncing back from an equal marble, foam only for weight, slow car makes the louder bang, and a parked car has moving energy.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid text grade 2.8 and adult 5.2, inside 6.5 and 9.5. Kid paragraphs use marbles, ramps, crashes and play dough in short sentences. Canvas banners wrap to at most three short lines at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler patterns and the explanation is under 12% shingle overlap with 443 (kinetic energy), 534 (naming types of energy), 106 (energy stores) and 432 (rolling down slopes). Each kid paragraph does one job: energy passes on, faster means more, energy spreads into sound, heat and shape, and bouncy versus squashy plus padding.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 × 640 (2x) in light and dark, before and after Show me, for all six steps. The first sheet showed the crash hotspots overlapping, the 30 cm ramp label under the banner and the bounce heights under the footer; the scene was re-laid out, the ramp shortened and the drop scale moved up, and the second sheet shows every label clear. Ramp dots and balls have 48 px hit areas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas drag or tap has a button twin (Roll gently or hard, From 10/20/30 cm, one button per crash clue, Drop each ball, each bumper). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the rolls tried, ramp results, clues found, bounce heights and bumper outcomes. The browser gate ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations and no console errors. Animations shorten to near-instant under reduced motion.
